title: DEALING WITH ANNOTATOR DISAGREEMENT IN HATE SPEECH CLASSIFICATION
findings: The paper's main findings are methodological, focusing on handling annotator disagreement in hate speech classification. It found that incorporating data with annotator disagreement, rather than discarding it, can improve model performance. Strategies like taking the minimum label value (Min strategy) were effective for binary classification on a dataset that includes hate speech targeted at religious groups, among others. The study achieved state-of-the-art results for hate speech detection in Turkish.
